mainTopic: Why a thief who slaughters on שבת, for עבודה זרה, or a שור הנסקל may be exempt or liable, including רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's ban on מעשה שבת and the defense of רבי מאיר
overview: The גמרא explains why a thief who slaughtered a stolen animal on שבת, for עבודה זרה, or as a שור הנסקל could be exempt. The exemption follows רבי שמעון: a שחיטה that does not make the meat permitted is not called שחיטה. That fits עבודה זרה and שור הנסקל, but a משנה says a שחיטה done on שבת is valid. The גמרא answers that this view follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, who forbids food made by breaking שבת on purpose to everyone, forever. His source is רבי חייא's teaching on 'כי קודש היא לכם'. 'קודש' forbids eating, 'לכם' still allows benefit, and 'מחלליה מות יומת' limits the rule to someone who did it on purpose. רב אחא and רבינא argue whether this ban is from the Torah or only from the חכמים. According to the rabbinic view, the חכמים exempt the thief only in the other cases. The גמרא then defends רבי מאיר, who makes the thief pay. For עבודה זרה, רבא says the man worships only at the end of the slaughter. For the שור הנסקל, רבה sets the case in a שומר's house and relies on the rules of רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון. Finally, רבה begins a new reading in which the thief slaughtered by himself, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The opinion follows רבי שמעון: improper slaughter is not slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the opinion that exempts the thief: it follows רבי שמעון, who holds that a שחיטה which does not permit the meat is not legally a שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי שמעון, who said: a slaughter that is not fit is not called a slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question by saying who this opinion follows: רבי שמעון. In his view, a slaughter that does not make the meat permitted does not count as slaughter at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief pays the extra ארבעה וחמשה only if he slaughtered the stolen animal. If that 'slaughter' does not legally count as שחיטה, he never did the act that makes him pay extra. So רבי שמעון's rule explains why he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not fit, meaning it does not make the meat permitted to eat
It is not called that; it does not count legally

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole rest of this section is about whether שחיטת שבת fits this rule of רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon, who said:
a slaughter that is not fit
is not called a slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from before this section by naming who the opinion follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the opinion to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was not clear why the thief should be exempt when he really did slaughter the animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי שמעון, a slaughter that does not permit the meat is not legally a slaughter, so he is exempt.

steps.title: But slaughtering on שבת is a valid slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's rule works for עבודה זרה and שור הנסקל, but a שחיטה on שבת makes the meat kosher, as a משנה states.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for עבודה זרה and an ox that is stoned. But slaughtering on שבת is a fit slaughter! As the משנה teaches: someone who slaughters on שבת or יום הכפורים, even though he is liable to death, his slaughter is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. רבי שמעון's rule fits two of the cases, but not the case of slaughtering on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal slaughtered for עבודה זרה, or a שור הנסקל, is forbidden to eat, so its שחיטה is 'not fit.' But a משנה says that meat slaughtered on שבת is kosher, even though the person who did it deserves death. So the שבת case is a fit שחיטה, and רבי שמעון's rule cannot explain why he is exempt there.

keyTerms.meaning: That works well (for this case, but...)
An ox sentenced to stoning for killing a person; its meat is forbidden
He is liable with his life (the death penalty)

phrases.english: This works well for idolatry and the ox that is stoned,
but slaughter on Shabbat
is a fit slaughter!
As we learned: one who slaughters on Shabbat or on Yom Kippur,
even though he is liable with his life,
his slaughter is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְשׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל, אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 1 for one of its three cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון's rule explains all the cases, including שחיטה on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that שחיטה on שבת is valid, so it is a 'fit' slaughter and should count as שחיטה.

steps.title: This opinion follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this opinion holds like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, for whom food made by breaking שבת is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in one short line. The source for this answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה that calls שחיטת שבת valid is not everyone's view. If the opinion follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, then meat slaughtered on שבת on purpose is forbidden. That makes it a 'not fit' שחיטה too, so רבי שמעון's rule works again.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Yoḥanan HaSandlar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the opinion to a תנא who disagrees with the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שחיטה on שבת is always valid, so it does not fit רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, food made on purpose on שבת is forbidden, so the שחיטה is 'not fit.'

steps.title: The ברייתא about cooking on שבת: three opinions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings three views about food cooked on שבת. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר forbids food cooked on purpose to everyone, forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: someone who cooks on שבת: by mistake, he may eat it; on purpose, he may not eat it. This is רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: by mistake, he may eat after שבת; on purpose, he may never eat it. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says: by mistake, others may eat it after שבת, but not he; on purpose, it may never be eaten, not by him and not by others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא where רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's opinion appears, to show his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each view gets stricter. רבי מאיר allows food cooked by mistake and forbids eating food cooked on purpose. רבי יהודה also restricts the mistaken case until after שבת, and forbids the deliberate case forever. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר forbids deliberate food to everyone forever. So by his view, an animal slaughtered on purpose on שבת is forbidden meat, a 'not fit' שחיטה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר: food made on purpose on שבת is forbidden to everyone forever. Food made by mistake may be eaten after שבת by others, but not by the one who made it.

phrases.english: As it is taught: one who cooks on Shabbat,
if by mistake, he may eat it;
if on purpose, he may not eat it;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
if by mistake, he may eat it after Shabbat ends;
if on purpose, he may never eat it.
Rabbi Yoḥanan HaSandlar says:
if by mistake, it may be eaten after Shabbat
by others, but not by him;
if on purpose, it may never be eaten,
not by him and not by others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן הסנדלר forbids food made on purpose on שבת, to everyone and forever
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about someone who cooks on שבת

steps.title: What is רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's strict ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוחנן הסנדלר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן הסנדלר forbids food made on שבת. This sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking שבת is a sin, but that alone does not show that the food made by it becomes forbidden. The גמרא wants a source that turns the food itself into something forbidden.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yoḥanan HaSandlar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion quoted in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה for forbidding food made on שבת

steps.title: רבי חייא: שבת is called קודש, so its products may not be eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא learned from 'כי קודש היא לכם' that just as קודש may not be eaten, things made by breaking שבת may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא taught at the entrance of the נשיא's house: 'And you shall keep the שבת, for it is holy to you.' Just as קודש is forbidden to eat, so too things made on שבת are forbidden to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רבי חייא's teaching. The פסוק calls שבת 'קודש,' so the rule of קודש is applied to things made on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison works like this: the תורה uses the word 'קודש' for שבת. Things that are קודש (holy property of the מקדש) may not be eaten by an ordinary person. So food made by breaking שבת also may not be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained a פסוק and taught a law from it
At the entrance of the house of the נשיא
Holy property, belonging to the מקדש

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya taught
at the entrance to the house of the Nasi:
“And you shall keep the Shabbat,
for it is holy to you”;
just as something holy is forbidden to eat,
so too things made on Shabbat are forbidden to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְדָרֵישׁ רַבִּי חִיָּיא אַפִּיתְחָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק calls שבת 'קודש'; just as קודש may not be eaten, things made by breaking שבת may not be eaten.

steps.title: Then benefit should also be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: If the comparison to קודש holds, then benefit should also be forbidden, since benefit from קודש is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so: just as קודש is forbidden for benefit, things made on שבת should also be forbidden for benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison further. If שבת's products are like קודש, maybe all benefit from them is forbidden, not just eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קודש is forbidden in two ways: eating and any benefit (הנאה). If the פסוק compares שבת to קודש, why should we copy only one of them? Logic says both should apply.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (the comparison should go further)
Benefit of any kind, not only eating

phrases.english: If so: just as something holy is forbidden for benefit,
so too things made on Shabbat should be forbidden for benefit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the comparison of step 6 should go.
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the comparison to eating only
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קודש is forbidden for benefit too, so a full comparison would also forbid benefit from things made on שבת.

steps.title: 'לכם': benefit is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The word 'לכם' teaches that things made on שבת remain yours for benefit; only eating is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'to you': it shall be yours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from an extra word in the same פסוק. 'לכם' ('to you') shows that you may still benefit from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say just 'it is holy.' It says 'holy to you.' 'To you' means it stays yours to use. So the comparison to קודש covers only eating, not benefit.

phrases.english: The verse states: “to you”;
it shall be yours.
phrases.notes: Meaning you may still use it and benefit from it; only eating is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison using a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Things made on שבת would be forbidden for benefit, like קודש.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לכם' teaches that benefit is allowed; only eating is forbidden.

steps.title: Maybe even by mistake?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ban should apply even when the person broke שבת by mistake, as קודש is forbidden in every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could it be even by mistake?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another question about the comparison: maybe even food made by mistake is forbidden. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קודש is forbidden no matter how it reached you. So if שבת's products are like קודש, maybe the intention of the one who made them does not matter. But רבי יוחנן הסנדלר allowed food made by mistake (for others, after שבת), so a source is needed.

phrases.english: One might think, even by mistake?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a second limit on the comparison of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between שוגג and מזיד in רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison to קודש does not depend on intention, so it should forbid even what was made by mistake.

steps.title: 'מחלליה מות יומת': only on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק continues 'those who break it shall be put to death,' which speaks only about someone who did it on purpose. So the ban on eating applies only to מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Those who break it shall surely be put to death.' I told you this about on purpose, not by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the end of the same פסוק. The death penalty applies only to someone who breaks שבת on purpose, so the whole rule is about him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links 'holy to you' with 'those who break it shall be put to death.' Only a מזיד gets the death penalty, so the comparison to קודש is limited to a מזיד. This matches רבי יוחנן הסנדלר: food made on purpose is forbidden forever, while food made by mistake is not fully forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall surely be put to death

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר's source is 'כי קודש היא לכם': 'קודש' forbids eating, 'לכם' allows benefit, and 'מחלליה מות יומת' limits it to מזיד. That is how שחיטת שבת on purpose becomes a 'not fit' שחיטה, which fits רבי שמעון's rule.

phrases.english: The verse states: “Those who break it shall surely be put to death”;
phrases.notes: שמות 31:14, the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: about one who did it on purpose I told you this,
and not about one who did it by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison using the end of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even food made by mistake on שבת would be forbidden, like קודש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only food made on purpose is forbidden to eat, since the פסוק speaks of someone who gets the death penalty.

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about the level of the ban
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא disagree: one says the ban on מעשה שבת is from the Torah, the other says it is from the Rabbis.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא and רבינא argue about this. One says the ban on food made by breaking שבת is from the Torah. The other says it is only from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement about the ban on eating food made by breaking שבת: is it a Torah law or a rabbinic law?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the derivation of רבי חייא sounded like a Torah-level ban. Now two אמוראים argue about it. One accepts it as Torah law, and the other says the Torah does not forbid it at all, only the Rabbis do.

phrases.english: Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it:
one said: the product of a שבת violation is forbidden by Torah law,
and one said: it is forbidden by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how strong the ban is that was just derived and narrowed in Steps 6-10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether the ban on מעשה שבת is Torah law or rabbinic law.

steps.title: The source for each side
steps.stepSummary: The Torah view relies on רבי חייא's reading. The rabbinic view reads 'קודש היא' as saying that only שבת itself is holy, not what is made on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it is Torah law relies on what we said before, from רבי חייא. The one who says it is rabbinic reads the פסוק 'it is holy' to mean: שבת itself is holy, but the things made on it are not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of each side of the disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same words, 'כי קודש היא'. The Torah side compares what is made on שבת to קודש. The rabbinic side stresses the word 'היא' (it): only שבת itself is holy, so its products are permitted by Torah law and forbidden only by the Rabbis.

keyTerms.meaning: Its products, the things made on it

phrases.english: The one who says it is Torah law: as we said,
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי חייא's lesson from 'כי קודש היא לכם'.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר דְּרַבָּנַן — אָמַר קְרָא: ״קֹדֶשׁ הִיא״,
phrases.english: the one who says it is rabbinic: the פסוק says, 'It is holy'
it (שבת) is holy, but its products are not holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for each side of the dispute in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rabbinic view learns from 'היא' that only שבת is holy, not its products.

steps.title: Why do the חכמים exempt the thief?
steps.stepSummary: If the ban is only rabbinic, the slaughter on שבת works by Torah law, so why do the חכמים exempt the thief who slaughtered on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the ban is only rabbinic, what is the reason of the חכמים who exempt the thief?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rabbinic view using the earlier ruling about a thief who slaughtered on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים exempt a thief who slaughtered a stolen animal on שבת from the extra payment. If, by Torah law, food made on שבת is fully allowed, then his slaughter was a fully valid slaughter. So why should he not pay for it?

phrases.english: And according to the one who says it is rabbinic,
what is the reason of the חכמים, who exempt?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier case of a thief who slaughtered on שבת: רבי מאיר makes him pay, and the חכמים exempt him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּרַבָּנַן מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּנַן דְּפָטְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rabbinic side of the dispute in Steps 11-12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that מעשה שבת is forbidden only by the Rabbis
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By Torah law the slaughter is valid, so the חכמים' exemption of the thief has no basis.

steps.title: The חכמים only exempt in the other cases
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים' exemption was not about שבת. It was only about the other cases: slaughtering for עבודה זרה and a שור הנסקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the חכמים exempt, they exempt only in the rest of the cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים never exempted the thief who slaughtered on שבת. They only exempted him in the other cases on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbinic view can admit that the חכמים agree the שבת slaughterer pays, because his slaughter counts by Torah law. Their disagreement with רבי מאיר is limited to the other cases.

phrases.english: When the חכמים exempt, it is on the rest of the cases.
phrases.notes: 'The rest' means slaughtering for עבודה זרה and slaughtering a שור הנסקל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the disagreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים exempt the thief in all the cases, including שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים exempt only in the other cases, not for slaughtering on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the view that the ban is rabbinic, everyone agrees the thief pays for slaughtering on שבת. The argument is only about the other cases.

steps.title: Slaughtering for עבודה זרה: the animal is no longer the owner's
steps.stepSummary: Against רבי מאיר: once the thief starts slaughtering for עבודה זרה, the animal becomes forbidden, so the rest of the slaughter is not done on the owner's animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who slaughters for עבודה זרה: as soon as he cuts a little, the animal becomes forbidden. So when he slaughters the rest, he is not slaughtering the owner's animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges רבי מאיר, who makes a thief pay even when he slaughters the stolen animal for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra payment is for slaughtering the owner's animal. But the very first cut for עבודה זרה makes the animal forbidden for any benefit, so it is worthless and no longer the owner's. The slaughter is completed on an animal that does not belong to the owner, so why should the thief pay?

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters for idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: This question is against רבי מאיר, who makes the thief pay, not against the חכמים.

phrases.english: One who slaughters for עבודה זרה:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דִּשְׁחַט בֵּיהּ פּוּרְתָּא — אִיתְּסַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: once he slaughtered it a little, it became forbidden;
so when he slaughters the rest,
it is not its owner's animal that he is slaughtering!

steps.triggerLanguage: טוֹבֵחַ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כֵּיוָן דִּשְׁחַט בֵּיהּ פּוּרְתָּא אִיתְּסַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from שבת to one of the other cases mentioned in Step 14 and questions רבי מאיר's ruling there.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that one who slaughters for עבודה זרה must pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal becomes forbidden at the first cut, so the slaughter is finished on an animal that no longer belongs to the owner.

steps.title: רבא: he worships only at the end of the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the case is one where the thief said he is worshipping only at the end of the slaughter, so the animal stays permitted until then.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this is talking about someone who says that he worships with it only at the end of the slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by describing a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person says ahead of time that his act of worship happens only when the slaughter is finished, the ban starts only at the end. So the whole slaughter is done while the animal is still the owner's, and the thief must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end of the slaughter

phrases.english: רבא said:
It is a case where he says that only at the end of the slaughter does he worship it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בְּאוֹמֵר בִּגְמַר זְבִיחָה הוּא עוֹבְדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal becomes forbidden at the first cut.
steps.terutzMaskana: He intended to worship only at the end of the slaughter, so the ban starts only then.

steps.title: The שור הנסקל: it is not his
steps.stepSummary: Against רבי מאיר: a שור הנסקל is already forbidden for benefit, so the thief is not slaughtering an animal that belongs to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ox that is to be stoned: it is not his ox that he is slaughtering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר again, this time about the case of a שור הנסקל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an ox is sentenced to stoning, no one may benefit from it, so it is worthless and belongs to no one. A thief who slaughters it is not slaughtering the owner's animal, so why should he pay?

phrases.english: The ox that is to be stoned:
it is not his ox that he is slaughtering!
phrases.notes: 'His' means the owner's. The ox no longer really belongs to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל לָאו דִּידֵיהּ הוּא דְּקָטָבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second of the other cases and questions רבי מאיר there, as Step 15 did for עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that one who slaughters a שור הנסקל must pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sentenced ox is forbidden for benefit and has no owner, so slaughtering it is not slaughtering the owner's animal.

steps.title: רבה: the ox was with a שומר
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the ox had been handed to a שומר. It did damage, was sentenced, and was then stolen, all while at the שומר's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: what case are we dealing with here? The owner gave the ox to a שומר. It caused damage at the שומר's house, it was sentenced at the שומר's house, and a thief stole it from the שומר's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge by setting up a very specific case. The גמרא will go on to explain how this case works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה does not say the ox is permitted. He places the whole story at the שומר's house: the damage, the sentence and the theft. This special setup is what explains רבי מאיר's ruling that the thief pays. The next step explains why it helps.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
A guardian who was given the animal to watch

phrases.english: רבה said: what case are we dealing with here?
For example, where he (the owner) handed it to a שומר,
and it caused damage while at the שומר's house,
and its sentence was finalized while at the שומר's house,
and a thief stole it from the שומר's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן כְּגוֹן שֶׁמְּסָרוֹ לְשׁוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sentenced ox has no owner, so slaughtering it cannot make the thief pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case involves an ox in a שומר's care, and this special setup will explain the payment.

steps.title: The two opinions behind the case of the ox held by the שומר
steps.stepSummary: רבה's case works because רבי מאיר agrees with רבי יעקב (a שומר may return a sentenced ox and be free) and with רבי שמעון (something that causes a money loss counts like money).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר holds like רבי יעקב and like רבי שמעון. Like רבי יעקב, who said that even after the ox was sentenced, if the guardian returns it to the owners, it counts as returned. And like רבי שמעון, who said that something that causes money is treated like money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the case from the last step (a sentenced ox stolen from a שומר's house) makes the thief liable according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יעקב, a שומר who returns the sentenced ox whole owes the owner nothing. Once the thief slaughters it, the שומר can no longer give it back and must pay the owner. According to רבי שמעון, an ox that saves the שומר from paying counts as having money value, so the thief damaged something of value.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that causes money gain or loss, even if it has no value of its own

steps.whatToRemember: A sentenced ox is forbidden for benefit and has no value of its own. It still has value for the שומר, because having it lets him return it and avoid paying the owner. That is why the thief who slaughters it can owe money.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ox itself became valuable again. It stays forbidden for benefit. Its 'value' is only that it protects the שומר from having to pay.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how רבי מאיר's ruling can apply even to an animal no one may benefit from. Two separate rules from other תנאים are combined to make it work.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir holds like Rabbi Yaakov,
and holds like Rabbi Shimon.
He holds like Rabbi Yaakov, who said:
Even after its sentence was finalized,
if the guardian returned it to its owners, it counts as returned.
And he holds like Rabbi Shimon, who said:
Something that causes money is considered like money.
phrases.notes: Here the ox causes money because without it the שומר has to pay the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב, וְסָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבה's case in step 18, showing why the ox has value for the one it was stolen from.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Grounding the case in two other תנאים' rules
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sentenced ox is forbidden for benefit, so it seems to have no owner with a money interest, and the thief should owe nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון, the ox has money value for the שומר, so the thief who slaughters it owes payment.

steps.title: רבה begins a new explanation: the thief slaughtered by himself
steps.stepSummary: רבה opens a different way to read the ברייתא: it is talking about a thief who did the slaughtering himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Actually, the ברייתא is talking about one who slaughters by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new explanation of the ברייתא from רבה. The section stops in the middle of his sentence, and the rest continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different explanation from the earlier one, in which רבי יוחנן read the ברייתא as a case where someone else slaughtered for the thief. רבה says the thief slaughtered himself. How this fits the ברייתא will be explained in the words that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (used to bring in a different explanation)
By himself, not through someone else

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Actually, it is talking about one who slaughters by himself,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם בְּטוֹבֵחַ עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the line built on slaughtering through another person and starts a new reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (the thief slaughtered himself)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was explained as a case where someone else did the slaughtering for the thief.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה reads the ברייתא as a thief who slaughtered by himself. His full reasoning continues in the next section.
